Senses.Explanation: Literally 'the feeling/state of doubt' (疑 doubt + 情 feeling, condition). In these texts it is what the cited texts say arises when a word or saying is raised for investigation (話頭, ‘word or saying’), and the texts describe it in bodily terms — knotted on the brows, impossible to put down. Boshan (Wuyi Yuanlai) defines it outright: 'when exerting effort, what matters is raising the doubt; and what is the doubt?' (做工夫貴在起疑情。何謂疑情？) — 'born, you don't know whence you came, so you cannot but doubt your place of coming; dead, you don't know where you go…'; when the pivot of life and death will not break, 'the doubt suddenly erupts, knotted on your very brows; you can't put it down and can't drive it off' (疑情頓發，結在眉睫上，放亦不下，趂亦不去), until one morning you 'smash the ball of doubt' (撲破疑團). Its measure is the stock line 'great doubt, great awakening; small doubt, small awakening; no doubt, no awakening' (大疑大悟，小疑小悟，不疑不悟). Dahui ties it to life and death: 'if the doubt is not broken, life and death press in' (疑情不破。生死交加). Gaofeng recounts his own case: brooding on 'the myriad things return to one — where does the one return?' (萬法歸一。一歸何處), 'from this the doubt suddenly erupted, so that I could not tell east from west, could not tell south from north' (自此疑情頓發。直得東西不辨。南北不分). The same graded formula reached Xueyan Zuqin as the advice that struck him — 'to investigate Chan you must raise the doubt; small doubt, small awakening' (參禪須是起疑情。小疑小悟) — spoken to him by Librarian Lai of Chuzhou (處州來書記) and preserved in Xueyan's general address (普說). In these texts the doubt is a felt mass — knotted on the brows (結在眉睫上) and held until it bursts (撲破疑團) — not ordinary doubting of this or that. Dahui's record carries the rationale as a saying: 'students today mostly do not doubt themselves — they doubt others; hence the saying: under great doubt there is necessarily great awakening' (今時學道者多不自疑。却疑他人。所以道。大疑之下必有大悟, T47n1998A). The Discourse on Forging in the Chan Gate (禪門鍛鍊說) quotes the graded maxim and sets the word against mere phrase-holding: 'the ancients said: great doubt, great awakening; small doubt, small awakening; no doubt, no awakening. So if the doubt is at ten parts, the awakening is at ten parts. And there are those in the world who teach people to hold the saying dead without raising the doubt — this is the great disease of investigating Chan' (古云：大疑大悟，小疑小悟，不疑不悟。故疑有十分，斯悟有十分。而世有教人死守話頭，不起疑情者，此參禪大病也, X63n1259). Its absence is a live interview topic — Ruo'an asked: 'when the doubt does not arise, what then?' — the master: 'what principle have you seen?' (箬庵問：「疑情不起時如何？」師云：「汝見甚麼道理？」, J25nB171) — and Boshan's letters diagnose it: 'the doubt not arising is the life-and-death mind not being urgent' (疑情不起是生死心不切, the Essential Collected Sayings of Great Master Boshan Wuyi 博山無異大師語錄集要, J27nB197).
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense, belonging to the vocabulary of looking at the saying (看話): the word travels with 'raise the doubt' (起疑情) and the word raised (話頭). Strongly multi-source across Linji-line masters — Dahui (the earliest witness here), Gaofeng of his line and Gaofeng's teacher Xueyan — plus the later Caodong master Boshan, who gives the explicit definition. Widely attested (208 allowlist texts). The witnesses from 'Spurring Advance through the Chan Barrier' (禪關策進) are from an anthology, but each section head names a master (verified: 'Chan Master Gaofeng Miao of Tianmu instructs the assembly' 天目高峯妙禪師示眾 = Gaofeng; 'the general address of Chan Master Xueyan Qin of Yuanzhou' 袁州雪巖欽禪師普說 = Xueyan) — though the Xueyan witness's specific line is speech reported inside his general address (普說), the advice of Librarian Lai of Chuzhou (處州來書記), so that occurrence carries a null MasterName. Zen-allowlist grep counts: the doubt (疑情) 936 hits in 208 of 462 texts; 'raise the doubt' (起疑情) 121, 'the doubt suddenly erupts' (疑情頓發) 62, 'the doubt unbroken' (疑情不破) 13, 'the doubt not arising' (疑情不起) 12; the companion 'ball of doubt' (疑團) 288 ('break the ball of doubt' 破疑團 92); the graded maxim's members 'no doubt, no awakening' (不疑不悟) 32, 'small doubt, small awakening' (小疑小悟) 29, and Dahui's 'under great doubt there is necessarily great awakening' (大疑之下必有大悟) 3 (T47n1998A, T47n1999, X70n1392).

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Boshan's Chan Admonitions (博山禪警語; the author line reads 'spoken by Yuanlai of the Ming' 明 元來說 = Boshan Wuyi Yuanlai). An explicit in-corpus definition — 'when exerting effort, what matters is raising the doubt; and what is the doubt?' — answered by the born-whence / dead-whither wondering.

Occurrences.Kwic: 則疑情頓發，結在眉睫上，放亦不下，趂亦不去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Boshan's Chan Admonitions (博山禪警語), same admonition, next lines: the bodily description — the doubt erupts and is 'knotted on the brows' (結在眉睫上), can't be put down or driven off. The textual basis for the 'felt mass / ball of doubt' rendering.

Dahui's Recorded Sayings (大慧語錄), in the letter answering Vice-Director Lü Longli (答呂郎中隆禮). Dahui on the doubt (疑情): unbroken, life and death press in; broken ('if the doubt is broken' 疑情若破), the life-and-death mind is cut off.
